challenges.name: internal-data-server-quiz
challenges.title: Who is asking, and how much comes back?
challenges.description: Two tools from the codedev-content MCP server: where the learner's identity should come from, and whether a clamped limit with a cursor keeps one result bounded.

questions.explanation: False. Schema validation checks the shape of an argument, not whether the caller may use it: "u_1093" is a perfectly valid user id, so the call passes validation and the handler returns another learner's progress. The model chose the id from text the user typed, which is exactly the input you cannot trust. The fix is to remove userId from the tool, take the user from the authenticated connection (the host's session or the OAuth token of the streamable HTTP request), and authorize every read against that identity on the server. The misconception is that a strict schema is an access control.

True. The handler clamps limit to the range 1..20 whatever the model asks for, cuts every snippet to 200 characters and never returns lesson bodies, so the size of one result has a fixed upper bound; the 5000 in the log was silently reduced to 20 and the rest is reachable through nextCursor, one bounded page at a time. Fetching limit + 1 rows is how the code knows whether a next page exists without counting every match. The misconception is that pagination only matters for the database; for an agent it also bounds the tokens a single tool result can push into the context window.
